fields.title: About this site
fields.description: How these docs are built with Mortar, and how editing them in your browser works.

data.source:
These docs are a Mortar site in the repository's `docs/` folder. Everything you read is content: try **Edit this page** at the bottom of any guide.

## Collections and bricks

- **`docs`**: each guide, with a title, a description, a section and a position for the sidebar, and a body.
- **`pages`**: pages outside the guides, such as the home page.

The bricks are **Markdown**, **Callout**, **API entry** (an export from the generated reference), and, on the home page, **Hero** and **Cards**.

## The API reference

The [reference](/reference) is generated from the packages' TypeScript sources and comments. A script runs TypeDoc over every public entry and writes a JSON file that the site renders:

```sh
pnpm reference
```

Run it after changing an exported API. A test fails if an export is missing from the reference.

## Editing in your browser

The published content is JSON in `docs/content/<collection>/<slug>.json`, bundled into the app. The server renders it, so every page arrives with its content in the HTML.

In the browser, the admin saves through `createContent` over the [session storage store](/docs/writing-a-store): nothing is sent anywhere. Every page reads through a content source with a version signal. Once a page has hydrated, it checks whether this tab has edits, and if so bumps the version, so every read runs again against the session storage store and your edits replace the published content.

While you have edits, a bar at the top of every page says so. **Reset to the published site** clears the session storage key and bumps the version again, so everything returns to what's published. The admin starts afresh too.

## Running it

```sh
pnpm docs          # dev server on port 3100
pnpm --filter mortar-docs build
```
